podcast.title: Lamentable State of Sid Baret in Late 1967 Concerts
podcast.body: By late 1967, during the height of Pin Floyd's activity, Sid Baret's condition in live performances was described as "very lamentable." Recordings from these concerts are said to be shocking, revealing his poor state, which was also evident in catatonic appearances during television interviews in the United States. "Tenemos grabaciones de conciertos que te dejan con la boca abierta del mal estado en el que estaba."

podcast.title: Emotional Impact of Sid Baret's 1975 Appearance
podcast.body: Sid Baret's shocking appearance in the studio during the recording of "Wish You Were Here" in 1975, where he was completely shaven, pale, and lacked eyebrows and eyelashes, had a profound and lasting impact on the band. Roger Waters was reportedly brought to tears, and the event changed the band's life and history forever. "Roger Waters rompía llorar totalmente desgarrado por el estado en el que estaba Sid Baret. Se quedaron tan impaltados que su vida y la historia de la banda cambiaría para siempre."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Continued Contact and Financial Support for Sid Baret
podcast.body: Following Sid Baret's 1975 studio appearance, Roger Waters re-established contact with his family, maintaining it until Sid Baret's death. In 1978, when Sid Baret ran out of money, Pin Floyd made gestures, including re-editions and securing rights, to ensure he received royalties as a full member. This allowed Sid Baret and his entire family to live comfortably without financial worries for the rest of his life. "Estos gestos económicos de Pin Floyd a Sid Baret permitieran que Sid Baret pasaría al resto de sus vidas sin tener que preocuparse del dinero y además que toda su familia entera pudiese para que haya de vivir sin preocuparse del dinero."

podcast.title: David Gilmore's Recruitment
podcast.body: David Gilmore was chosen to replace Sid Baret, not by chance, but because he was a childhood friend of both Roger Waters and Sid Baret. Although other names like "Jetpack" (likely a mispronunciation of Jethro Tull's Ian Anderson) were initially considered, Gilmore's existing relationship with the band members provided a stable environment. The initial idea was for Sid Baret to remain a stable member for composition and recording only, similar to "the Beatles," but his condition made it impossible. "Realmente se optó por David Gilmore porque era un amigo de la infancia de Roger Waters y Sid Baret."

podcast.title: Early Success Driven by Sid Baret
podcast.body: Pin Floyd achieved rapid success in its early years, primarily due to the immense talent of Sid Baret. However, even during this initial period, Sid Baret was already experiencing severe mental health issues. "todo el éxito de Pin Floyd al principio estaba detrás del talento de Sid Baret pero ya de aquella Sid Baret estaba muy mal."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Sid Baret's Post-Ejection Pursuit
podcast.body: After his expulsion from the band, Sid Baret compulsively pursued Pin Floyd, attending their concerts and even showing up at EMI recording studios, attempting to enter through fire exits. There's an anecdote of him chasing the band to Ibiza, appearing at the airport "almost in tatters running," which highlighted the tragic nature of his continued connection to his former friends. "Tenemos un episodio en el que Sid Baret fue a perseguir a la banda. Pin Floyd hasta Ibiza y apareció en el aeropuerto casi en Carlson Cillos corriendo, intentando coger a la banda."
